lyrics:
[Intro: lone acoustic guitar, kick drum on every beat]

[Verse 1: raspy male voice, urgent]
I wandered off on a Tuesday, nobody saw me go
Thought I'd find a better field, a higher hill, I don't know
By dark I was down in a gully with my leg caught in the thorns
Thinking nobody counts that close. Nobody comes this far.

[Chorus: banjo, stomps, gang vocals]
But you were one short of a hundred
And you wouldn't call it close enough
Left the whole flock on the hillside
Came down through the rocks and the rough
Ninety-nine were safe and sleeping
And you came after one
One short of a hundred
And I'm the one

[Verse 2: voice closer, band holding back]
I heard you before I saw you, calling out my name
Not "where have you been," not "you ought to be ashamed"
You got down in the ditch with me, tore your hands on the vine
Put me up on your shoulders like I was some great find

[Chorus: banjo, stomps, gang vocals]
'Cause you were one short of a hundred
And you wouldn't call it close enough
Left the whole flock on the hillside
Came down through the rocks and the rough
Ninety-nine were safe and sleeping
And you came after one
One short of a hundred
And I'm the one

[Bridge: building, everyone shouting by the end]
And the story goes you sang the whole way home
Called the neighbors, threw a party, 'cause the one was not alone
Good Shepherd, that's the name you gave yourself
Laid your life down for the sheep. Jesus, no one else.

[Final Chorus: full band, loudest]
You were one short of a hundred
And you wouldn't call it close enough
Left the whole flock on the hillside
Came down through the rocks and the rough
Ninety-nine were safe and sleeping
And you came after one
One short of a hundred
And I'm the one

[Outro: stomps fade, one voice alone]
And I'm the one.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 96 BPM, 4/4, G major. A stomping folk-rock march that starts with one guitar and ends with a crowd.

VOICE: Male tenor, raspy and earnest, pushing hard in the choruses. A gang of men and women shout-sing every chorus with him. The bridge climbs until he is nearly yelling. The last line is alone and quiet.

INSTRUMENTS: Strummed acoustic guitar, a kick drum on every beat, banjo, upright bass, floor toms and tambourine, mandolin, a trumpet line in the last chorus, foot stomps and handclaps.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and kick. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:44 Chorus 1 with the gang. 1:16 Verse 2. 1:46 Chorus 2. 2:16 Bridge, building. 2:44 Final chorus. 3:16 Outro, stomps fade, the solo line at 3:24.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2010s stomp-and-holler folk rock: acoustic, loud, roomy, voices slightly ragged on purpose.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The gang entering on 'one short of a hundred' at 0:44.

THE REVEAL: Verse 1 is someone lost in the dark. The first chorus at 0:44 brings in a flock and a hundred, which churchgoers will know at once; for everyone else the bridge at 2:16 says 'Good Shepherd' and the name.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Lost, found, carried, celebrated.
